checks.finding: Actors, states, inputs and outputs are concrete enough that two implementers would build the same behaviour. The CLI (requirements.md:232-238), the sixteen-row diagnostic table (:409-426), the exit-code contract (AC-013), the step (0)/(a)-(m) processing order (:263-395), the enforcement-derived-field set (:480-508), and the direct-write-vs-journaled-transaction split (:358-395, Main Workflows 4, Roles and Permissions :1052-1067) each resolve to one reading. Two Minor imprecisions were weighed and do not meet the bar: (1) requirements.md:347-350 says 'Every Block in REQ-002's sixteen-row taxonomy satisfies this predicate except the two REQ-002 names AC-012 excepts' -- but both excepted ids (disabled-legacy-invocation, the Evidence-itself sub-case of output-schema-validation-failed) do leave no publication artifact standing and therefore do satisfy the stated predicate; the 'except' belongs to the consequence clause (which Evidence record is written), not the predicate, and the actual behaviour for both is fixed unambiguously elsewhere (AC-012, Main Workflows 4 'written directly', Roles and Permissions). (2) AC-041 requires 'one independently-triggerable fixture per ... two rows' while TEST-041 enumerates four combinations (lite x {legacy-seven-layer, facet-hybrid, facet-native}; full x lite-three-file), leaving 2-vs-4 fixtures open; the Block behaviour itself is identical across all four, so this is a fixture-count clarification, not a behavioural ambiguity.

The tenth test suite is simultaneously mandated and declared unscheduled. acceptance-tests.md:75 (AC-026/TEST-026) states: 'the tenth pair, resolve-project-context-caller-contract.tests.sh/.ps1, is deferred and not scheduled by this package (tasks.md "Deferred, not scheduled"; traceability.md likewise counts nine)', narrowed 2026-08-27 under ruling D(2). Four other statements of the same fact contradict it and were not updated: (a) acceptance-tests.md:21-27, the preamble of the same file, says 'design.md's own Test Strategy names ten suites this feature's future tasks.md schedules authoring ... keeping the suite count at ten'; (b) requirements.md:736-784 (REQ-006) requires the test design to cover 'at minimum, the ten items design.md's own Test Strategy fixes at contract level' and names 'a live-SKILL.md caller-contract suite (design.md Test Strategy item 10, REQ-007 ...) asserting non-invocation while Context-absent, single-invocation on Context-present, Block-surfacing on a REQ-002 Block, and a position-sensitive anchor-fingerprint drift check'; (c) AC-027 (requirements.md:939) requires 'design.md Test Strategy items 1-10' present under tests/fixtures/capability-resolver/; (d) TEST-042 (acceptance-tests.md:88), TEST-046 (:92) and TEST-053 (:99) each name tests/resolve-project-context-caller-contract.tests.sh/.ps1 as their Test Target and each carries Status 'Planned' with no deferral note, unlike AC-026 whose Status row does carry one. A grep of both documents shows 'deferred'/'tenth'/'nine (suites)' occurs at exactly one site, acceptance-tests.md:75. Downstream failure mode: the task author cannot decide whether to author that suite (REQ-006/AC-027 require it; TEST-026 says tasks.md does not schedule it), and the verifier cannot close AC-027, AC-042, AC-046 or AC-053, because their only named vehicle is declared out of the package's scope -- the identical 'criterion unsatisfiable by the frozen task package' shape TEST-026's own parenthetical was written to remove. This belongs to specification review, not implementation or task review: both halves are Phase 1 statements (a Goal and an Acceptance Criterion) inside the two frozen documents this gate reviews, and the acceptance-tests preamble declares a 1:1 AC<->TEST mapping 'in both directions'. Critical severity is justified because it renders four acceptance criteria impossible to satisfy within this package and leaves REQ-006's own stated minimum coverage unmet, which is the calibration's 'impossible acceptance criteria' class.

Two material paths implied by the requirements have no test that can actually be run. (1) REQ-007's caller-integration failure modes -- the Resolver never being invoked while a Project Context is absent or derives disabled-legacy (AC-042), a REQ-002 Block surfacing to the interview session rather than silently degrading (AC-046(c)), and the position-sensitive anchor-fingerprint drift check that guards OQ-003's resolution (AC-046(d)/AC-053) -- are covered only by tests/resolve-project-context-caller-contract.tests.sh/.ps1, the suite acceptance-tests.md:75 declares deferred and unscheduled. The on-Block non-degradation path is the one REQ-007 grounds in decision document v2 section 7's fail-closed principle, and requirements.md:1511-1518 (Risks) relies on AC-053's fixture 'failing immediately, not silently' as the mitigation for anchor drift; with the suite unscheduled, that mitigation has no vehicle. (2) AC-009 (requirements.md:921) requires that 'across each of the three non-Blocking required_lite_checks-sourcing states ... advisory-missing ..., required-present-empty ..., and zero-match ... the written capability-summary.yaml validates successfully', while its 1:1-mapped TEST-009 (acceptance-tests.md:58) provides fixtures for only two of the three and states the third 'has no automated fixture -- Epic A2's own lite_policy schema (additionalProperties: false, sub-keys {eligible, upgrade_reasons} only) admits no required_lite_checks key on any real Capability entry today, so a fixture exercising it would not itself pass validate-capability-registry', adding 'No synthetic-Registry-extension fixture is used for any of the three states'. The criterion therefore demands demonstration of a state its own test row proves cannot be constructed, and forbids the only construction that could produce it. Downstream failure mode: a task author must either build an impossible fixture or silently treat 2-of-3 as satisfying 'each of the three', and a verifier cannot close AC-009 either way. This belongs to specification review because the package's own repair convention for exactly this shape lives in these two documents -- AC-016 explicitly excludes the branch it cannot test, and AC-026 was narrowed from ten to nine on 2026-08-27 for the same reason -- and AC-009 is the site that convention was not propagated to. Major, not Critical: the underlying product rules are unambiguous and the uncovered Lite state is genuinely unreachable until an out-of-scope Epic A2 schema revision lands, so the defect is an over-claiming criterion and a missing test vehicle rather than a contradiction in the Resolver's behaviour.

All three Assumptions (requirements.md:1377-1400) carry an explicit resolution path rather than an open dependency: the four sibling contracts landing unmodified with a named follow-up obligation if they change; the protected-suffix reservation being re-verified at Phase-2 start with a stated alternative sequencing if it is not yet live; and the SKILL.md unprotected status explicitly labelled 'a live-repository snapshot, re-verified at the future implementation task's own start time, not a permanent guarantee'. Open Questions are dispositioned: OQ-001 and OQ-002 are deferred to a named future caller/epic with the deferral itself recorded as a Non-goal, and OQ-003 is marked resolved with a concrete file:line anchor plus a drift check. The Risks section assigns owners rather than leaving gaps unowned -- notably the Epic A2 Registry-schema revision, named as 'an explicit, owned prerequisite for Epic A6's required-enforcement Lite path' with owner, scope and migration stated (requirements.md:137-163, :1426-1456). investigation.md carries a conforming '## Amendment Re-Review Context' entry meeting the calibration's full evidence bar (full commit hashes, per-document SHA-256 including the 12fd1241 set whose requirements.md/acceptance-tests.md values match this round's pinned hashes, verbatim dated human approvals of 2026-08-23/2026-08-24, and commit-or-hash citations for every later-phase artifact referenced), so the phase-sequencing suppression applies and no finding here rests on the mere existence of later-phase artifacts.

Every human-approval, governance and irreversible-change boundary in scope is stated and testable. Protected-path writing: script code is staged under specs/<feature>/human-copy/ for human application via apply-human-copy and is 'never a direct agent write to the live path' (requirements.md:1041-1051), with the scope corrected so generated artifacts are excluded from that route; the no-plugins/** boundary is locked by AC-032/TEST-032. Human action is named where it is required: AC-026's Status reads 'Planned (Status resolves through a human cp action for the test.yml portion)' with a staged candidate and MANIFEST.sha256 entry. The irreversible-change boundary is the strongest case and is correctly fail-closed: an unconvergeable publication journal triggers no automatic repair at all, leaves every interrupted target other than resolver-evidence.yaml exactly as found for manual operator intervention, and Blocks publication-journal-recovery (requirements.md:1253-1279, :1341-1349), with AC-047 requiring both halves of that state in one fixture and explicitly recording that asserting either half alone would contradict AC-012. disabled-legacy-invocation is a fail-closed refusal with no code path that produces a Facet Manifest while the pipeline is derived-inactive (Security Boundaries :1297-1305), locked by AC-015 and AC-042. No boundary is asserted without an observable check.

The product behaviour a design reviewer would otherwise have to invent is present. The processing order is fixed step by step including the mandatory step-(0) crash-recovery scan and the (l)/(m) recheck-then-publish sequence; the ambiguity-Block taxonomy is a closed sixteen-row table with per-row trigger conditions rather than the ad hoc enumeration the Problems section says would otherwise be invented at implementation time; the two orchestration rules with no upstream owner -- multi-component union matching and predicate-instance-keyed facet-name aggregation -- are stated with their aggregation semantics, ordering and reason-population rules and are explicitly flagged as this feature's own new decisions for spec-time evaluation (:1457-1468). Output shapes are bound by reference to already-frozen Epic A4 schemas plus one new contract whose fields, cardinality bindings, bidirectional-consistency rules and diagnostics severity cardinality are fully specified (REQ-004). Note that this PASS is about product behaviour only: the CONTRADICTION and EDGE-CASE-COVERAGE failures above concern the verification plan's scope, and the design reviewer will need the caller-contract-suite conflict resolved before task decomposition, but neither requires inventing Resolver behaviour.
